For three hundred years the Gorbulon clans have ruled Zotov as the Empire's enfeoffed nobility. Gorbulons maintained a sprawling feudal hierarchy of vassal houses, tributary corporations, and indentured labor worlds, all owing fealty (and ossite) to the Gorbulon high seat on Gorb.

Not all is well fo rteh sons of Gorb. Their once unstoppable fleet in the sector now gutted. Roughly 60% of Gorbulon capital ships were lost or crippled during the galactic civil war. What remains is old, undercrewed, and spread thin garrisoning ossite refineries. The Dominion compensates by leaning hard on vassal levies (Flubbadite included, on paper) and mercenary contracts it can increasingly ill afford.

Officially they are still Gorbulon tributaries. In reality they stockpile warships, cultivate Imperial court contacts of their own, and calculate exactly how long they can wait before the Gorbulons' weakness becomes undeniable enough to break the oath outright.

While officially under Imperial naval command. It is practically an autonomous military governorship personally loyal to Admiral Zakar. wk_156_gt7t.body:
A comfortable mid-tier processing world, refining crude piped in from the smaller Flubbadite fields.

It is known for its deadly flora and fauna that lurk outside the gates of its settlements.
wk_156_gt7t.title: Hupp

wk_157_o8ei.body:
Named for the perpetual haze thrown off its surface refineries, Ashfall is a solidly prosperous industrial world of mid-size cities and well-paid guild labor. 

Its refinery unions are influential enough that the Flubbadite Council courts them directly.
wk_157_o8ei.title: Ashfall

wk_158_kxa7.body:
(formerly Imperial Garrison Station Zotov-9) 
This is the 11th Fleet's forward operating base, informally renamed by its own crews.
Technically it is Imperial property. Functionally it is Zakar's personal seat of power in the sector.
it boasts one of the largest shipyards in the sector.
wk_158_kxa7.title: Zakar's Station

wk_160_7hbb.body:
A mid-sector world seized under "stabilization" authority after a Gorbulon-Flubbadite border dispute turned violent. Now it is permanently garrisoned by the 11th Fleet
This is the first Zotov world to answer to Zakar alone, and a template for more.
wk_160_7hbb.title: Cordage Reach

Brilliant, magnetic, unburdened by sentiment. Zakar is the Most famous man in the empire. He made his name at Putting down rebellion in the Makovy Sector winning a chain of 4 stunning, if costly victories over the rebels. No individual is more responsible for the end of the civil war than he is. 

He Now commands the 11th Fleet and is quietly building a power base independent of the Imperial chain of command.

wk_195_gz3t.body:
The Galactic Empire has just weathered the greatest crisis in its history. A rebellion in the Makovy sector brought the empire to the brink of collapse. In the end the imperial forces and their vassals prevailed at great cost, Imperial power has receded and many local lords vie for wealth and power in the far corners of the galaxy.

The Zotov sector avoided the mass death and destruction of the rebellion, but many of its fleets were ravaged fighting for the empire far from home during the conflict. In the years since the rebellion, the empire has left many of its outposts in the region in the control of the house of Gorb, directly occupying only a few key strategic systems. 

But all is not well for the gorbulons. Their own fleet was severely diminished during the war and they are increasingly relying on the ships of their unruly vassals to fill out their fleet. Seeing this weakness, the council of Flubb, historically one of the gorbulons most powerful vassals, have made a play for greater galactic power, refusing to cooperate with gorbulon officials. Conflict seems inevitable.

In the midst of this brewing conflict the Empire sent its most famous citizen, the war hero Admiral Zakar to administer the sector and bring peace. But the Admiral is as ambitious as he is cunning and With the 11th imperial fleet under his personal command he stands poised to make a play for power himself.
wk_195_gz3t.title: The Zotov Sector Today

wk_196_9d0c.body:
The gate to the Empire. A heavily trafficked Gorbulon waystation. Most convoys bound for the capital pass through its lanes, and the Vega Reserve fleet keeps a standing watch here.

This is Ossite's last stop before it is shipped ot the imperial core
wk_196_9d0c.title: Vega Gate

wk_2928_zsrc.body:
The Fubbaldite Seat of power. The sectors second great ossite field, tapped only two generations ago. 

The world is fast becoming a metropolis utilizing the newest, most efficient extraction methods. it won't be long until it surpasses even Gorb at this rate
wk_2928_zsrc.title: Flubba

wk_2929_flgi.body:
The Homeworld of the Gorbulons and their political capital.

Ring-cities and clan citadels built over the sector's first and richest ossite fields. Visibly declining Towers stretch as far as the eye can see.
wk_2929_flgi.title: Gorb

wk_2931_diau.body: The largest world controlled by the Children of Luuk. Eden is vital to the faiths autonomy. While Luuk's rest is the spiritual home of the movement, it is a barren world incapable of supporting a large population. Eden on the other hand is lush and fertile. It is unusually bereft of Ossite for the region and is this unpolluted by the industry.
wk_2931_diau.title: Eden

wk_2941_ac4x.body:
The old power. For three hundred years the Gorbulon clans have ruled Zotov as the Empire's enfeoffed nobility. Gorbulons maintained a sprawling feudal hierarchy of vassal houses, tributary corporations, and indentured labor worlds, all owing fealty (and ossite) to the Gorbulon high seat on Gorb.

Not all is well fo rteh sons of Gorb. Their once unstoppable fleet in the sector now gutted. Roughly 60% of Gorbulon capital ships were lost or crippled during the galactic civil war. What remains is old, undercrewed, and spread thin garrisoning ossite refineries. The Dominion compensates by leaning hard on vassal levies (Flubbadite included, on paper) and mercenary contracts it can increasingly ill afford.

Gorbulon power is spread thin an vulnerable but when they can mobilize their vassal fleets they still command teh most numerous FFleet in the sector.
wk_2941_ac4x.title: Gorbulons

wk_2942_9kue.body:
Once a cluster of minor mining tributaries, the Flubbadites are now the sector's rising industrial power. Their wealth was untouched by the worst of the Civil war, sitting on the second-largest ossite basin, and increasingly unwilling to pretend they still answer to Gorb.

Officially they are still Gorbulon tributaries. In reality they stockpile warships, cultivate Imperial court contacts of their own, and calculate exactly how long they can wait before the Gorbulons' weakness becomes undeniable enough to break the oath outright.

United in purpose, their smaller but more modern fleet punches above its weightclass in the sector. and unlike the Gorblulons or the Imperials they can fully rely on their forces loyalty
wk_2942_9kue.title: Flubbadites

wk_2944_zmy0.body:
The Children are refugees turned settlers. Descendants of the followers of the prophet Luuk, who led their ancestors to Zotov's outer worlds generations ago after exile from their homeworld in the imperial Core. They are the sector's oldest continuous population. There is no world in the sector without Luukite communities. 

The original Luukites made their home on Eden and maintain an independent, though small, fleet there
wk_2944_zmy0.title: Children of Luuk

wk_2945_kjyp.body:
Nominally an Imperial garrison force. In practice, the only fully intact, first-rate battle-fleet in Zotov Sector, and the personal instrument of a commander with no intention of staying a policeman forever.

The 11th fleet has no history in the Zotov Sector and is free to enforce imperial will so long as the ossite continues to flow.

While officially under Imperial naval command. It is practically an autonomous military governorship personally loyal to Admiral Zakar. Admiral Zakar has spent three years quietly filling sector administrative posts with officers loyal to him personally rather than the Fleet chain of command, and cultivating the ossite-dependent Imperial bureaucracy back home as a source of leverage rather than orders.
wk_2945_kjyp.title: The 11th Fleet

wk_78_llkg.body: Bobursk is one home to an old imperial outpost that had been left vacant for a generation. It had become a hub for organized crime in the sector. One of the first initiatives undertaken by admiral Zakar was to clear out the mob from the system, an act which won the admiral much love from the local populace.\n\nAfter installing personnel loyal to him alone it is one of the few systems unwaveringly loyal to the 11th Fleet.
wk_78_llkg.title: Bobursk
